issues.description: The problem statement and solution use the function name build_msd_circ(...) but the template defines build_msd_circuit(...). This name mismatch is structural: students following the problem text or tests (which expect build_msd_circ) will not find the expected function in the template, causing confusion and test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template API match the problem statement and solution. Rename the template function build_msd_circuit to build_msd_circ with the same signature and docstring, or add a thin compatibility wrapper in the template: def build_msd_circ(*args, **kwargs): return build_msd_circuit(*args, **kwargs). Ensure tests and documentation consistently refer to build_msd_circ.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution implementation refer to the distillation-construction function as build_msd_circ, but the template code provides a stub named build_msd_circuit. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entity (the function that builds the magic-state distillation circuit) creates a direct mapping barrier for students: tests and instructions will reference build_msd_circ while the starter file defines build_msd_circuit, causing confusion and likely test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template stub from build_msd_circuit to build_msd_circ so the template, problem statement, and solution consistently use the same identifier (or, alternatively, update the problem/tests and solution to use build_msd_circuit). Ensure all references in tests and documentation match the chosen name.
